note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Hard domains motivate tool-augmented annotator, evaluated in target, out-of-domain and adjacent domains

nodes.name: Annotation is hard in factual, coding, math domains
nodes.description: For responses with long-form factual, advanced coding or math content, both AI and many human annotators struggle to give reliable pairwise judgements, often falling back on superficial features such as style.

nodes.name: Tool-using Evaluation Agent framework
nodes.description: The framework augments existing AI annotators with (1) an initial domain assessment selecting tools, (2) tool execution (web-search fact check, code-execution code check and math check), and (3) a final decision, using structured JSON output.

nodes.name: Fallback to baseline outside tool domains
nodes.description: If the initial domain assessment finds no tool useful, the agent reverts to the baseline annotator, to avoid regressions on non-target domains.

nodes.name: Existing datasets are saturated
nodes.description: Some RewardBench subsets are saturated, with state-of-the-art LLM-as-a-judge systems near 100% agreement, so new pairwise datasets (LongFact pairwise, GSM8k hard pairwise, APPS pairwise) were created.

nodes.name: Fact-check agent improves long-form factual annotation
nodes.description: Augmenting any baseline with the fact-checking agent improves agreement on long-form factual pairs, e.g. GPT-4o pick-best 63% to 81% and ArenaHard 78% to 80% (Fig 4).

nodes.name: Math results are mixed
nodes.description: On GSM8k hard pairwise, agents outperform only some baselines, ArenaHard outperforms all agent-based methods, and overall agreement stays around 56% (Fig 5).

nodes.name: Better on RewardMATH
nodes.description: On RewardMATH the method outperforms the ArenaHard baseline (App H).

nodes.name: Code execution greatly improves coding annotation
nodes.description: On APPS, the agent improves GPT-3.5-Turbo from 31% to 71% and ArenaHard from 38% to 72% (Fig 6).

nodes.name: Baselines prefer incorrect GPT-4 code on APPS
nodes.description: Baseline annotators perform worse than random on APPS, preferring the correct response only 26% to 42% of the time, possibly due to self-enhancement bias; the code-execution agent shows no such bias.

nodes.name: Minimal out-of-domain regression
nodes.description: On out-of-domain RewardBench categories (Chat, Chat Hard, Safety) agreement drops by less than 2% for all baselines (Fig 7).

nodes.name: Adjacent domains show mixed effects
nodes.description: On adjacent saturated domains, short-form fact checking and simple math improve consistently while simple coding (HumanEval) decreases by up to 9% (Fig 9).

nodes.name: Tools are a complexity/cost trade-off
nodes.description: External validation tools often improve annotation quality, strongest for advanced coding, but trade off complexity and cost and may not suit every use case.

isolated_nodes.name: Hyperparameters strongly affect baselines
isolated_nodes.description: Baseline annotator configurations such as the prompt have a strong impact on performance, and a simple GPT-4o 'select the better' annotator is competitive on many datasets (Sec 4.3.1, Obs 2).

structural_reasoning: Motivation and framework design lead to dataset creation and domain-wise results, summarized in a cost-benefit conclusion.
